Sam (customer): Hey, we rotated an org API key a few minutes ago and now when teammates switch to project 'ad-processor' in the console they immediately see a 403. API requests using the same key still work for other projects. Error in console: 'Forbidden: insufficient scope'. Repro steps below.

Anya (support): sorry about that — can you paste the exact error text and the steps you used to rotate the key?

Sam (customer): Sure. Steps: 1) Settings -> API keys -> rotate key (chose 'keep scopes'). 2) Copied new key, shared with team. 3) Two users click org -> Projects -> ad-processor and see 403.

Sam (customer): Console error (copy): ``Forbidden: insufficient scope (code: auth.scope_mismatch) request_id=8f3a2b``

Sam (customer): API call that still works (curl):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_newkey" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/ad-processor/models
```

Luis (eng): odd. Do you have the scope list from the new key (the token metadata)? if you can run: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_newkey" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/_internal/token_meta` and paste the response that helps.

Sam (customer): Pasting response: ``{"scopes": ["inference:read", "embed:read"], "org_id": "org_73", "created_by": "sam@example.com"}``

Anya (support): thanks — console expects `console:org` or `console:project` scopes for UI actions. Looks like rotation somehow trimmed the console scopes. Did you choose any restricted preset during rotation?

Sam (customer): No, I used the web UI rotate button and kept the defaults. The old key had `console:org` and `inference:read` in the metadata (we checked it before deleting).

deploy-bot: Deployment event: service/identity-svc v2.3.8 rolled out 18s ago to us-west-2

Ida (sre): FYI we had a small migration that touched token projection earlier today; might be related.

Luis (eng): ok reproducing locally: when a key is rotated via the UI and the user has a pending projection migration state, console scopes can be dropped if the backend path takes the 'scopes_from_profile' branch. Likely a bug. Creating a ticket.

Anya (support): For an immediate workaround, you can: 1) generate a new key from Settings -> API keys and select 'Full console access' (or check console scopes) OR 2) re-add `console:project` scope via the API admin endpoint (if you have org admin). Example: 
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scopes": ["inference:read","console:project","console:org"]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org_73/tokens/rotate-meta?token_id=tok_abc123
```

Sam (customer): I don't have an admin token handy. We regenerated a key with full scopes and that fixed console access for the affected users. Thanks.

Luis (eng): Good. We're marking this as a bug (REDWOOD-12345). Root cause: migration flag + rotate UI path omitted console scopes. Patch ready, will be deployed in the next release window.

Anya (support): I'll keep this thread open until fix is deployed and will follow up with a postmortem. In the meantime, if any other customers hit this, ask them to reissue with console scopes or use the admin endpoint to restore scopes.

Sam (customer): Appreciate the quick response — workaround worked for us. Please ping when the fix lands. :thumbsup:

Ida (sre): Noted, will add monitoring alert for token-meta drift during rotation.

Anya (support): Ticket/Follow-up: REDWOOD-12345, escalation to eng-runtime.

Sam (customer): Closing on our side once you confirm patch — thanks everyone!
